reason: Plan Phase 3 static serving: an /api/* miss is a JSON 404 ({"error":"Not found"}) in Rust; Next answers the same 404 status with its HTML not-found page. Status is identical; only the body format changes, by design.
Same responses as api-miss-json-404: Next's HTML not-found page carries its page caching headers (ETag, private no-cache) that a JSON error does not; Rust sends no-store (api-no-store).

Review 2, finding 8: Rust marks every /api answer that sets no caching policy of its own as Cache-Control: no-store (they are often personal: token or secret in the request). TS sends no Cache-Control there. Only this exact pair (absent → no-store) is accepted.

RFC 9110 §15.5.6: a 405 must list the allowed methods. Next's App Router sends no Allow on 405; Rust sends it in Next's own OPTIONS format ("GET, HEAD, OPTIONS[, POST]"). Status and (empty) body are identical.

Requests that make the TS handler throw outside its try/catch (malformed JSON body, a string playerId) get Next's framework 500 with an empty body. Rust reproduces the same failure cases with the same 500 status and the same (absent) DB effect, checked by the mutation DB diff, but answers with the API's single error shape {"error":"Internal Server Error"} (crates/server/src/error.rs) instead of an empty body.
